title: Band-9 Samples: If you catch a cold, what do you do to help you feel better? [Why?]
passage_html:
This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 12 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 2 Test 1 question:

“If you catch a cold, what do you do to help you feel better? [Why?]”

Sample 1

When I get struck with a cold, I tend to lean toward the more natural healing methods. I find solace in resting and staying hydrated, as it helps my body recover in its own time. I’m not a big fan of medicinal pills, as I believe they can be harsh on the body. Instead, I trust my body’s inherent ability to recuperate.

Sample 2

When I find myself under the weather, my instinctive reaction is to engage in light exercise. It might sound counterintuitive, but I’ve found that gentle physical activities, like yoga or a brisk walk, can help clear congestion and increase my energy levels. Of course, I’m careful not to overdo it and listen to my body’s cues for rest.

Sample 3

When I contract a cold, I often resort to herbal remedies. I believe in their healing properties because they have been used for centuries. For instance, I make a concoction of ginger, lemon, and honey, which is renowned for its anti-inflammatory and immune-boosting properties. I also increase my intake of fruits rich in Vitamin C. This approach not only alleviates my symptoms but also provides a reassuring sense of returning to nature’s remedies.

Sample 4

When I’m under the weather, I prioritize rest above everything else. Our bodies need energy to fight off viruses, and nothing replenishes energy better than a good night’s sleep. So, I cut back on my daily activities, put on my comfiest pajamas, and snuggle up in bed with a good book. It might sound simple, but sleep works wonders in speeding up recovery.

Sample 5

In the event of catching a cold, I rely heavily on over-the-counter medications. Cold symptoms can be quite bothersome, and modern medicine provides rapid relief. I usually go for a combination drug that targets multiple symptoms, such as a runny nose, cough, and body aches. Although it might not cure the cold itself, it definitely makes the whole ordeal more bearable.

Sample 6

Whenever I get a sniffle, I double my fluid intake. Hydration is key in flushing out the virus from my system, so I constantly drink water, herbal teas, and clear broths. I’ve noticed that the increased liquid intake also soothes my throat and clears up congestion. It’s a simple yet effective way to expedite recovery.

Sample 7

Oh, when I’m down with a cold, it’s my perfect excuse for some relaxation and binge-watching. I believe that resting and distracting the mind with some good movies or TV shows can positively impact the recovery process. It might not directly cure the cold, but it certainly helps me feel better emotionally, and a positive mindset can make a difference too.

Sample 8

Whenever I catch a cold, one of my top comfort choices is indulging in warm soups and broths. Not only do they feel soothing on the throat, but they also provide essential nutrients and hydration. I like to prepare homemade chicken soup with lots of vegetables, as it offers a perfect combination of flavors and health benefits. It’s like a warm hug from the inside that helps me feel better and nourished during the recovery process.

Sample 9

In all honesty, I can’t recall ever having the sniffles or a sore throat. The secret, in my opinion, lies in a healthy lifestyle and impeccable hygiene habits. I always make sure to consume a nutrient-rich diet, exercise regularly, and get enough sleep. Alongside this, cleanliness plays a crucial role in warding off germs. So, that’s my formula for staying cold-free.

Sample 10

Well, it’s actually quite fascinating but I’ve never really had to deal with the usual symptoms of a cold. That’s primarily because I’ve always been a staunch believer in the power of preventive healthcare. So, I make a point to get flu vaccines every year. They’ve done wonders for me, not only keeping me safe from the common cold but also allowing me to live a more active and productive life.
